title: Rex Ryan set to appear on ESPN days after arrest for allegedly hitting pedestrians
content:
Rex Ryan is set to appear as scheduled on ESPN’s NFL studio coverage Sunday, days after he was arrested and accused of running over the feet of two pedestrians with his pickup truck in Nashville, Tenn.

A network spokesman confirmed ESPN’s plans for the analyst and former NFL head coach to return to its broadcasts.

“As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown,” a network statement read.

Ryan, 63, surrendered to authorities and was arrested on six outstanding misdemeanor charges Wednesday, a day after he allegedly struck the pedestrians on Nashville’s Broadway street and left the scene, according to the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department.

The police said Ryan hit the individuals, who suffered minor injuries, as they were crossing the street. The pedestrians had a walk sign when Ryan, who was turning from 4th Avenue, ran over their feet and made contact with one of their legs, the police said in a statement.

The victims said they caught up to Ryan at a stoplight. They said he got out of the car, argued with them, then got back in his vehicle and drove away.

The former New York Jets and Buffalo Bills head coach was charged with two counts of leaving the scene of an accident, two counts of failure to give information/render aid and two counts of failure to obey a traffic control signal.
